summary: E2E verification of new DELETE product + DELETE work-order features. Backend regression 121/121 GREEN (11 new TestP3DDelete tests confirmed via pytest -n 0). Frontend: (a) Admin (arif) sees red 'Hapus Produk' / 'Hapus WO' buttons with correct data-testids; (b) shadcn AlertDialog opens in Bahasa Indonesia with cascade+refusal warnings and red-600 confirm button; (c) Cancel is a true no-op (stays on page, no API call); (d) Confirm deletes -> success toast (sonner) + navigate to list; (e) after WO delete, GET /api/work-orders/{wo} = 404 and GET /api/operator-progress/{wo} = 404 (cascade OK); (f) after product delete, GET /api/products/{sku} = 404 and all 7 sub-collections + /work-instructions/{sku} = 404; (g) QC (leni) and Production (redi) DO NOT see either delete button anywhere; (h) seed RFL-AOD-H11-V1 remains fully intact (recipe=17, bundles=10, pin-map=3, common-mistakes=4, revisions=135). 409 semantics for WO-ref and child-version were NOT re-tested via UI in this iteration because they are fully covered by the 11 backend pytest cases (TestP3DDelete). The dialog warning text explicitly informs the user of both refusal conditions, so the frontend error-surface path is code-obvious (deleteProduct/deleteWo call toast.error(err?.response?.data?.detail) on catch, which is the standard sonner pattern used elsewhere in the app).

critical_code_review_comments: Positive: delete-product dialog copy is excellent — explicitly lists all 7 sub-collections that cascade, mentions the file_asset soft-delete semantics (storage safe), and warns about BOTH refusal conditions (WO ref + child version). This is a strong UX pattern.
Positive: delete-wo dialog similarly explains the cascade (batch_colors + qc + operator_progress + qc_evidence soft-delete). Users know exactly what disappears.
Positive: Admin-only gate is applied at BOTH the trigger button AND the AlertDialog wrapper, so non-Admins get zero UI surface — not just a disabled button.
Positive: red-600 destructive styling is applied on AlertDialogAction as required by shadcn destructive pattern.

Minor (non-blocking): batch-colors endpoint returns 200 with empty array even for deleted WO numbers (no existence check). Not a bug — the WO doc is gone, so batch_colors is empty — but for stricter API hygiene it could 404 like operator-progress does. Consistent behavior across cascade endpoints would be a nice polish, not a requirement.
Minor (pre-existing, non-blocking): routes.py is now ~1533 lines. Splitting into modular routers (products.py / work_orders.py / master.py) would improve maintainability.
